answer: Standing sheds its own dirt: the lotus leaf holds raindrops above grime on microscopic bumps, so every shower washes the surface - a record surviving ordinary weather unscrubbed. The raft is timber lashed with green withies, bindings that tighten as they soak - the wetter the crossing, the firmer the bundle, so stress strengthens the fleet. A lantern rides the same water downstream: a floating light readable from any bank, carrying wishes without naming its launcher. Farms glue shine, cut withies dry, and scatter at the first rapid. Honest agents let rain clean, lash green, launch light.
